metadata.school_name: The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

analysis.name: Adele Williams
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Williams was AMAZING! I took her Intro to Poetry class last semester, and I loved it. It was something different compared to my other classes, so I enjoyed learning about poetry a lot. The readings were pretty light, considering it was mostly poems. She does have reading quizzes, so be aware of that. She's super chill too.

I loved Adele so much! I was dreading taking ENGL 105 since I'm a junior transfer, and she made it not only bearable, but fun! I really enjoyed our class zoom meetings. She is just the nicest person - super chill and funny. I wish I could take more classes with her.

She is seriously the best teacher ever, I couldn't recommend a better English professor. She is so leniant and will work with you. Not a very strict grader and gives great feedback. There are a lot of papers, but that's literally all you do, and she gives you a lot of creative freedom. English has never been my favorite subject but she made it fun.

I took Writing in the Natural Sciences and found that I had more essays to write compared to my friends who took other ENGL 105 classes, but I don't regret it. She lets you write about practically anything that you want. I highly recommend attending her office hours at least once and she is understanding of absences and late work.

Dr. Williams is an amazing professor for English 105i! Attendance is mandatory but you get 3 unexcused absences before you start losing points. Assignments and readings can be long but you can write about anything you like. Participation is 20% of your grade, but if you turn in work and participate in discussions you'll get an A.

analysis.name: Benjamin Arbuckle
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 52 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Arbuckle is by far my favorite professor at UNC. I learned so much in this class, and he inspired me to add an ANTH minor. He is the nicest and most caring guy ever, and his lectures were always entertaining. I loved the day we did the scribal training, and the object biographies and the final project were cool and fun to work on. Take him!!!

Sitting in on Arbuckle's lectures is like story time for the class.  His enthusiasm and excitement for teaching the material rubs off on you, and this is being written by a science major & minor student.  Exams are easy to study for as long as you put in effort the night before or so & listen to the lectures generally.  GREAT class for gened reqs!

Best class ever! There were no midterms or finals. One 5 page paper in the middle of the semester, but not difficult if you don't leave it to the last minute. Professor Arbuckle is understanding and kind. While his lectures were not required, they were very interesting and worth your time to attend. Would 100% take a class with Arbuckle again.

kind, very interesting, understanding prof. easy A. 1 paper due in the middle of the year making it possible to actually be interested in the content. you get downgraded if you use AI but are given the (optional) chance to revise the paper at the end of the sem. this was good incentive to be more ambitious with the work resulting in an A.

Amazing class!! Professor Arbuckle is so nice and caring. He is accessible at all times of the day and often answers emails very quickly. He answers any and all questions. Professor Arbuckle's lectures are very interesting and sometimes showed images about his archaeology experience which was incredible to see first hand.

analysis.name: Adrian Drummond-Cole
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 43 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Adrian is a great guy who genuinely cares about teaching-unlike a lot of professors at UNC. The course content is stuff that really gets you to think. Getting an A or A- is very easy and manageable, but he makes you work for it and you have a learn a decent bit in order to, which is fair. Very fair gen ed and the grading was also fair.

I really liked Adrian (very understanding, funny, passionate) and the class was great (documentary every Friday, he basically covers the readings in class). Only complaint is while attendance isn't tracked, if you don't show up ur grade will drop. Easy class work, simple exams if you use the study guide, and plenty of extra credit!

As a STEM major I loved this gen ed, one of my favorite classes I've taken at UNC. Adrian is funny, honest, and super caring to all his students. The class is composed of "commonplace books" which are quick, not graded harshly at all, and kind of fun. The midterm was easy as well. You should try to do at least 30% of the reading.

Very easy and interesting class. No technology allowed but also no homework. That alone makes it less stressful than 99% of classes, and it's a bonus that the content is pretty interesting and useful as well. He's a very funny guy as well, super kind. Absolutely recommend any class he teaches.

Dr. Drummond-Cole is one of my favourite professors! He made a large class feel like a seminar by making space for discussions and creating really engaging participation exercises. The readings were super interesting and assignments were very doable. Just keep on top of the work and stay engaged in class.

analysis.name: Alexandrea Ravenelle
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: FYS worse than Organic Chemistry! Your weekly assignments will ask you to read 80 pages only to be brutally graded and torn apart with no justification. The utter disregard for rubrics will continue because your 50 percent final presentation will be graded as if an infant threw a dart and randomly hit a grade, which WILL effectively wreck your GPA.

She is extremely unclear in her grading feedback and your grade has absolutely no correlation with how much you participate during class, defeating the entire purpose of a "seminar" course. Zero consistency in grading across the board. She is insufferable and will do her best to make you fail, especially if you challenge her beliefs in discussion.

There is very little graded in actually participation which goes against the idea of a "seminar" class. Most grades comes from out of work readings. She grades very vaguely and harshly. Even if you were to follow the rubric word for word, the chances are you will get a grade much below what you are expecting.

Her lectures are funny, but she is generally a very passive-aggressive and not very understanding professor. Was very disrespectful during Creativity Relay presentations. My group had an issue because a student wasn't doing any work, and she was not very understanding or helpful. The class is easy, but she tries to make it unnecessarily difficult.

She makes her lectures entertaining, however she is really rude and passive aggressive during the creativity relay presentations, obviously aggravated and corrects the content students share immediately after their presentations. Grading is really harsh, its not a difficult class however the grading style makes it hard to get a good grade in class.

take_again_recent.note: Recent reviews are noticeably better than older ones.

analysis.name: Angelique Bassard
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Bassard is such a character, she is very funny and considerate. She has a lot of group projects, and there are pop quizzes on her lecture material. As long as you follow her rubrics and participate in class. Since it's a required course everyone has to take, it isn't the most fun material, but she makes the class more interesting.

Professor Bassard is quite a character. She is witty and humorous. I enjoyed taking English will her. The class is very lecture based, and we had pop quizzes. Some of the work felt like busy work at times. The readings didn't feel as relevant, but I recommend doing the readings. Overall great class!

Her class lectures are very easy to understand, and each class provides educational insight. She is very lenient with grading and will make any changes to the rubric if necessary. She is also humorous and will add in on class discussions. Her class does include group projects, so if that is something you like, definitely take this class.

She was so nice and supportive! You should go to office hours because she will help so much with your essays! She is also really funny and personable. The class is mostly participation and group work (other than 2 essays). I would definitely take this class with her again because she helped me grow as a writer!

I thought Prof. Bassard was really caring and passionate about teaching. She is very genuine and wants  a lot of participation from students, which is understandable. Good ENGL105 to take for freshmen, and she will answer any questions you have.

analysis.name: Abigail Panter
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. P is really awesome. She cares very deeply about her students and her class is not hard at all. I had no tests. She is an easy grader and wants you to do well (very flexible with deadlines). However, her lectures can be very long and all over the place. It's fine because no tests means you don't need to be fully attentive and can space off.

Dr. P is amazing and one of the best teachers I had this semester. She is always available during office hours and always checks in on students. The classwork is useful and not too difficult, with only a few hours of work outside of class each week. No exams.
Dr. P is the sweetest and truly cares about all of her students. Her class was interesting and the workload wasn't heavy at all.
Genuinely the best professor at UNC. I adore her she's perfect, she was there for me during a really hard time.
You can tell that Dr. Panter actually cares about her students and she makes her classes enjoyable. She wants students to succeed and if you put effort in and participate you will do well.

good_rating_recent.note: Recent reviews are noticeably worse than older ones.

analysis.name: Martha Alexander
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 50 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Sra. Alexander is phenomenal! She really cares about her students and wants them to succeed. Homework is limited and if you prepare for tests, you'll do great. She's always there to help you and with her help the class isn't too difficult.

Loved her class! So kind and felt like she cared about knowing us individually. Learned so much Spanish!! Challenging class but her workload is very manageable. Fav thing about her is that all of her quizzes are exactly what she said they would be, no trickery.
Martha was SUPER organized and always fair.  I really enjoyed her 203 class and would definitely recommend

Professor Alexander is super laid back and does not have heavy expectations. She doesn't expect you to be fluent in Spanish, and reviews a lot of key concepts. She grades very leniently, and she's very transparent about exam content. We spend most of class just working in groups; it's very low stakes, and casual. I would take her if you can!

Really great! I liked her a lot, she was super easy to talk to and was very excited about us learning! So sweet and make class very engaging and fun, we did a lot of great culture stuff too. Not difficult if you try and give it your best, just stay on top of the dates and you'll be a-okay!

analysis.name: Shorna Allred
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She is an AMAZING professor with engaging lectures! The readings are a lot but so interesting and even if you do not get to them you'll follow along in class just fine. She just wants students to share their thoughts and succeed, so students are graded by few things. Attendance is not mandatory but it is a small class so missing is noticeable.
Easiest class of my life, engaging lectures with frequent activities- I love Dr. Allred!!! We spent many class periods just taking nature walks :)

She is amazing. I took it for a seminar and we basically had no homework. I barely showed up to class and got an A. The final project where we gave a presentation for trees was so easy- I finished the entire thing in 2 days. She is super kind and understanding.  Take her if possible. Btw, attendance is only mandatory sometimes.

good_rating_recent.note: Recent reviews are noticeably worse than older ones.

analysis.name: Christoph Brachmann
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 38 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He is extremely knowledgeable and really makes you think. The other ratings that say need to know a lot about catholic/christian beliefs & history are right. I wasn't knowledgeable about this and had to learn a lot about it. He cold calls a lot, so do the readings but it was a very enjoyable class.

I really enjoyed this class; he knows what he is talking about. Before you write the paper, it is important to go to his office hours. But overall there is only 1 midterm, 2 papers and a final. However if you skip class, you will do badly because the questions for the exam come straight out of the discussions in class.
100s of paintings to memorize for final; lots of detail required. If the class wasn't graded I'd have loved it. Fascinating material & a very knowledgable professor. Expect a B.

Dr. Branchmann is incredibly knowledgeable about the topic and very entertaining. He relentlessly cold-calls, but he rarely cares about accuracy. The paper and essay aren't too difficult as long as you review the PowerPoint presentations, which are posted on Canvas. Participation and attendance are essential.

My favorite professor in UNC's art history department. Beneath a somewhat intimidating exterior, he is a very nice person and one of the smartest art history professors. His classes are discussion driven. Sometimes students ask questions he did not know the answer to. He makes a point to thoroughly investigate the question and report back to class.

good_rating_recent.note: Recent reviews are noticeably better than older ones.

take_again_recent.note: Recent reviews are noticeably better than older ones.

analysis.name: Bryn Werley
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof was a nice human but ended up missing 5.5 full classes due to illness before having to step down after exam 2. We were forced to learn unit 5 from various Ulas and one in person lecture with a sub. Made her exams ridiculously hard.

Avoid at all costs. This is easily the worst experience I've had at UNC. Her tests were insanely hard, lecturing skills were mid at best, and she missed 7.5/20 lectures. We were still expected to keep up with all of the content on our own. I would pick Beaver 100x over this. I cannot emphasize how bad this was, and exam medians were always failing.

Worst experience I've had in a chem class at UNC by far. Tests are a nightmare compared to other summer session professor's tests and she abandoned us a week leading up to exam 2 and finals. Whole class had to email to chem department try and resolve issues she refused to solve on her own. Avoid at any cost and wait for any other chem professor

Took this course during Summer Session II. At the time of writing this, she has missed 5 consecutive days of class, which is more than an entire unit during the summer timeline - during the worst unit. Didn't show up for the second exam but made it ridiculously hard after barely teaching us. So disrespectful of our time and money and so unfair.

Professor Werley is a nice person, but was not ready to teach an already difficult subject in an accelerated format. The professor stepped away due to illness and missed a large portion of our summer session, right before the second exam and the final. This left us underprepared, especially because the ULAs were not prepped either.

analysis.name: Anna Curtis
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 212 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: She is a very nice professor and passionate about chem, but unfortunately I could not follow her teaching style as the pacing was hard to follow. The exams are absurdly hard, and I felt very unprepared for all of them, but I do not think that is a fault of hers. I had her three times, and somehow it just kept getting worse.

Gen chem is standardized, so the professor doesn't really matter; however, I would say that Curtis is a good professor and teaches the material in an easily understandable way. I would just say come into the class knowing that it's going to be hard and that you'll have to put in a lot of time outside of class if you want to do well.

Curtis is one of those better Chem 102 profs as she helped explain concepts in depth and why calculations are done as is. Though the concepts aren't too bad, the exams are where they'll get you. I recommend getting as much help as possible through GPSS and CHEMpossible & try to go to her 6-min meeting at least once. She's cool!

The UNC chem department is tough, but Dr. Curtis does a great job teaching students the content needed to pass exams, and she does so in a way that is easier to understand than the textbook. Dr. Curtis is also a friendly person, and it is clear that she wants her students to succeed. Definitely take with Curtis if you can!

CHEM102 is standardized and I honestly think she is the best professor you can get. Sometimes she makes concepts confusing but she clearly does care and tries to make class fun. It's not an easy class, but I appreciate her efforts. She was also very kind about any questions in class.

take_again_recent.note: Recent reviews are noticeably better than older ones.

analysis.name: George Baroud
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Baroud seems really intense at first but honestly he is one of the most inspirational and passionate professors I've had. I took CLAS122 for the focus capacities and loved it so much I ended up taking 241 too. Classes are action packed and I always left feeling I learned something. Readings are manageable and exams are fine.

Prof. Baroud is easily one of my favorite professors. His class was immensely difficult (300 pages of dry, dense reading each week; could not bullshit your way through exams), but his grading was fair and he forces you to grow as a thinker/reader. He's scary (and maybe a bit snarky) at first, but he is super approachable in office hours.

Don't take this class if you want to sit by, skip the readings, and hope you'll get a good grade. Professor Baroud is an amazing professor, extremely intelligent, and loves the Roman Empire. Highly recommend going to office hours, as he wants to know every student personally. If you are willing to go a little crazy, then this is the class for you.

Quite literally the most engaging and thought provoking lectures I've ever heard. He's an incredibly knowledgable and charismatic professor. Main downside of the class are the reading assignments, almost too lengthy to handle. If you show up to all the lectures, do the readings, and ask questions, you'll do well. I wish I could take CLAS122 again.
Professor Baroud is an amazing storyteller and professor. I got a B and still would take the class again because of how well he taught the course.

analysis.name: Luc Bovens
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 51 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: What an absolutely FANTASTIC professor. The best prof. I have ever had at UNC. PLEASE take any class with him. He is hilarious, makes learning fun, and the tests are so straightforward. Go to your TA's office hours for help with the essays, and you will do really well. The test question bank is given to you to study before the exam!!

I like Prof. Bovens. He's clearly a very knowledgeable dude. It's easy to get an A in his class. I didn't really enjoy the class because I wanted more open discussion during lecture, but instead it was almost completely him reviewing the source materials. He presented great perspectives, but there wasn't really much opportunity to contribute.

Luc was my favorite professor I've had at UNC. Lectures were funny and easy to understand but you can tell he's a brilliant mind. Gives you plenty of resources to do well on tests and there was a video presentation in place of a final exam. Great class and great professor

Liked Prof. Bovens, his lectures were pretty interesting but not overly complicated for a minor intro class. Clear about expectations and had good office hours.
Eric Choi was my TA, we mostly just did practice problems during recitation & he graded a little tough at first, but gave great feedback that helped me do better on second paper and final.

choose TA Myreaka, who explained concepts so well and outlined midterm and final preparation perfectly to great grades on both. Her paper grading wasn't harsh yet still very helpful. Luc's lectures are great, though it can be easy to zone out in such a large class. Papers topics are up to you and weightage is balanced well with the midterm + final.

analysis.name: Emily Burkhead
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 254 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: The class itself is not horrible, you can preview by looking up "understanding analysis" and practice. Tests decide your grade, not hard if you know how to apply a theorem or prove it. She hates to grade higher for those who improved, and she grades harsh, bonus and curve are almost nothing, I regret taking her hunger game class only for a minor.

Taking Calculus 3 with this professor was the worst experience of my life. Studying for her exams brought me to tears. The test study guides are an extremely poor representation of the exams and she wrote most of the final so her students did bad on that too. Her class average is a C, while others are an A. Do not take this class! Save your GPA!!!

I gave her a 4/5 when I took her for MATH233. That was a lie. Tests and homework were graded harshly which would have been fine if she curved generously. Given what she said is "on track for an A/B/C" after each midterm, the curve should have been like +13% when it was actually +3%. Ragebait incarnate.

Carefully assess your abilities. There's no curve for this class at all. It's the only one among 233 courses that requires a weekly exam. Also, I've seen exams from other sections that had only five simple questions in 50 minutes, but Professor Burkhead's test contained more than 20 challenging and time-consuming problems, with no extra time given.

Save your grade and don't take 381 with Burkhead. Inaccessible and hard to approach with questions related to grading or asking her to explain concepts. Asked her many times to explain the material, and was often met with snarky remarks. Office hours are even worse, as she is not much help if you're lost.

good_rating_recent.note: Recent reviews are noticeably worse than older ones.

take_again_recent.note: Recent reviews are noticeably better than older ones.

analysis.name: Pauline Blaimont
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Blaimont is a great professor. Biology is not my strongest subject, and I struggled at times, but not due to her teaching. Exams are fair and reflect lectures, and homework aligns well. Attend class (Poll Everywhere helps), use office hours, and you'll do well. She responds to emails quickly.

Dr. Blaimont was amazing! This class had a lot of content and work, but her lectures and teaching style always prepared me. Her exams were difficult in the right ways, testing things in an understandable manner from lectures and work. 220 had a lot of content, but I feel like she made it as manageable as possible. Take her if you have the chance!

Dr. Blaimont was probably the best 220 professor ever. I was so terrified for this class and she was the nicest person ever. Her lectures were clear and engaging, and didn't mind explaining something slowly in class when I asked for help. Office hours are great, exams are fair, and she is hilarious! Don't miss the chance to take a class with her!

Blaimont is an amazing professor. She is very kind, very enthusiastic about the subject (she is young and relatively new), and very straightforward about what she wants from her students. She is also very accessible outside of class for questions, help, and anything else. 100% the best option to take for 220!

God-tier of a professor. Definitely take Dr. Blaimont for BIOL 220! Very fair exams and grading on assignments. Patient on answering questions. I wish she would answer questions more directly, but she is already doing an amazing job for her 1st semester at UNC! Study the ppt and journal club, then you will be fine!

good_rating_recent.note: Recent reviews are noticeably worse than older ones.

analysis.name: Shinjini Chattopadhyay
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I absolutely love Dr. Chattopadhyay; I enjoyed this class so much that I added an English minor! Genuinely cares about students and even asked if workload was too heavy (it never was). She made modernism so enticing that I read more works from authors we talked about in class.

I love Dr. Chattopadhyay! She is very knowledgeable and passionate about the material, and makes class interactive and exciting! As someone who normally struggles speak up in class, I found myself raising my hand for every question. She has reasonable expectations and is flexible with deadlines. I loved this class so much I added an English minor!

Loved her! So sweet, and you can tell she likes what she was teaching. Very easy assignments, readings, but lectures can get repetitive. If you have her, please raise your hand! Her eyes light up when people participate, and I found myself participating to make up for the fact that hardly anyone else did. Great seminar.

Such a sweet professor; the bulk of the work consists of readings, which can be a little challenging to understand due to the nature of the course. The work isn't too difficult, but it can get repetitive. The classes are usually the same (lecture on the book, then discussion), but the work is straightforward.

I loved taking ENGL 124 with Shinjini! She's clearly so passionate about what she teaches, and I genuinely enjoyed coming to class. It isn't difficult, and I learned so much about the course content since it was fun and immersive. I would definitely recommend taking a class with her.

good_rating_recent.note: Recent reviews are noticeably worse than older ones.

analysis.name: Joseph Compton
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 101 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Curved 2 midterms, then told us we were “cooked” right before starting the final, then dropped the curve entirely. No grading scale, no clear policy, and final scores hidden until grades were locked. Some secret points added to the final after complaints. Grading felt arbitrary, dismissive, and shady. If you value fairness, avoid this professor.

Took him for Calc 2 and really liked him, so decided to take for discrete and regretted it. I know discrete is supposed to be hard, but not this hard. Homework is impossible to do with going to office hours and/or using AI/internet (and even then still incredibly hard). Test questions are also unnecessarily difficult. Don't recommend taking him.

Professor Compton is a very good teacher, but the homework and tests just ruin it for me. The grading is unfair for how difficult the homework and tests are, and the difficulty did not help me learn more. You need to teach yourself all the homework and make this class a very high priority. Terrifying grader and hardest class in my life.

Difficult and time consuming homework, no practice exams or study guide, not clear on what he puts on midterms. Grading was harsh and unfair. He's fine in lecture, but makes the class entirely more difficult than it needs to be. Random quizzes to count for attendance & only drops one to account for sickness, so if you have to miss more you're SOL.

I'm not sure why he has good ratings on here... He is very condescending, which is not a productive enviornment for learning difficult subjects like math. He doesn't give any practice for exams. Also, you can do great and understand all the topics on midterms, but then do slightly bad on the final and it will tank your grade.

analysis.name: Connor McMahon
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 54 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Cece is an absolute legend. This class was difficult, especially towards the end but she made it fun. You do need to put in the work in this class to make a good grade but she provides many resources to help you. She is also very accommodating as well which I appreciate. Look forward to taking another class with her again!
Solid class, compared to other comp sci professors she definitely stands out as one of the most coherent ones. I don't see why anyone could dislike her. Any class she teaches I will sign up for.

Cece was my favorite professor this year. She was super accessible throughout the year, very accommodating, and really kind. The material is difficult especially towards the end of the year but Cece recognizes this and tries to be as fair as possible. She's inspirational to women in CS and I will take ANY classes she teaches in the future.

The 1 thing I have a critique abt is that a lot of class was learning by peers. She would do 1 problem and then gave us some to do the rest of class. I learn through multiple teacher-led examples, not my friends who are struggling and dont understand. I had to learn a lot on my own. Lectures not recorded, bad if you wanted to go over concepts.

I heard that 311 would be one of the hardest classes of the intro sequence, but she made it feel like the easiest since 110. Good and clear lectures that moved at a manageable pace, and the peer interaction made learning way easier and the class very enjoyable even though I don't really care about this field of CS that much.

analysis.name: Elizabeth McLaughlin
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 455 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: do not trust her, she wont give any partial credit EVEN when you deserve it! i self studied everything for the final and ended up doing well ONLY because of that

While very knowledgeable and willing to answer questions, the professor's teaching style was rushed and felt unfit for students learning brand new content. The homework was very hard and not useful for tests. However, the TAs and ULA were super helpful.

Dr. McLaughlin doesn't follow lesson plans or the syllabus schedule. She puts little effort into teaching, but has intentionally harder exams than other professors and refuses leniency (i.e. dropping the lowest midterm) unlike other professors. She is passive-aggressive about people not coming to class, even though she knows her lectures are bad.

Heard shes great for Math-232+ but do not. DO NOT take her for math-231. Shes horrible at teaching the material and KNOWS it and makes the exams insanely hard that even TAs have trouble explaining the material. Told TAs to "grade harshly" to spite students that didn't come to class. Go to another profs lectures to learn. Take exams when needed.

After taking AP Calc and MATH130, I had a fair understanding of the topics, but after Mclaughlin, I have never been more confused about calc. After having near-perfect attendance for the first two midterms, I decided it was a waste of time to continue attending. She makes new notes for each class period and has not followed her posted curriculum.

good_rating_recent.note: Recent reviews are noticeably worse than older ones.

take_again_recent.note: Recent reviews are noticeably better than older ones.

analysis.name: Jocelyn Chua
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 81 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: It wasn't a bad course but it seems like she was more interested in discussing the use of AI in her course. She seemed to be looking extensively for AI usage. I'm not kidding when I say that the study guides covered not to use AI for this course on a whole page. Other than that, it was a fair course and she is sweet.

Good lecturer, had zoom class option because class was put all the way in kenan flaggler.  Around ~4 books for the course, some being ethnographies that were easy reads and interesting (did not ask super in depth questions on the book content).  6 Reading Responses throughout the semester that needed to be ~1 page long, 1 midterm, then the final.

Dr. Chua's class was enjoyable. Make sure you show up (or watch) the lectures as well as do the readings. The midterm and final exam make up most of your grade, but as long as you go to/watch lecture, and even just skim/know what the readings are talking about, you should do well on these exams.

You get 3 free unexcused absences, but each additional one drops your grade by one third of a letter grade.

I really enjoyed this professor's class. He created an engaging and enjoyable learning environment, with a strong balance between lectures and independent work. The workload was reasonable, and his teaching style made the material easy to understand, which made it much easier to succeed in the course.

Super nice and funny guy. Very down to earth. So approachable and an overall great resource to have on campus in terms of interview prep and overall life advice. Definitely a lot more work than other ENGL 105 classes, but it was interesting to me and I think I became a better writer.

No homework, so make sure you keep up with the readings and it is not too hard

Prof. Goldstein is a gem.  He offered review sessions outside of class before exams and stayed as late as students had questions.  His section of the course is 100% exams, but exams were very fair and he doesn't try to trick you like other bio profs do.  Extra credit offered and genuinely cares about student well-being and learning.

Never before have I been so shortchanged and so enthralled by a class. Best CHEM prof at UNC!!! She is very caring and has a sense of humor. She is also very kind and explains everything clearly and patiently, like your grandma. The 2nd exam was difficult but I know it wasn't written by her. Her exams were the easiest orgo exams I've taken! Take her orgo she's the best!

Prof Eskew was supposed to teach my class all semester, but randomly took off for the first month. I had Prof Zurcher, and she was amazing. Then Eskew came back and my grade tanked. She's just such a boring lecturer, and she doesn't explain anything. When people ask questions, she doesn;t actually answer them and just moves on.

Dr. Eskew was very kind and approachable, often making an effort to connect with students in class despite it being a large lecture. Her slides were well put together, and she explained things clearly. Exams are tough, but that is to be expected from orgo. Just do the homework and practice problems, and you should be fine. Best orgo professor!

Dr. Eskew is kind, patient, and caring. This class is like 90% outside practice and 10% lecture, which is expected. She made Organic Chem II feel far less intimidating than I thought it would be. Definitely nail down NMR, as it appears on every exam. Her exams (unlike Beavers) are actually fair. Would definitely recommend! Such a sweetheart!

Easy class in general, reading quizzes and midterm + final paper. TAKE THIS CLASS WHILE AT UNC

She's a great and lenient professor! Loves to talk, easy A. Weekly journal (one page). 1-2 question quizzes, usually true or false, with 2 attempts. Very low stakes class. One group presentation. She's very funny, does random activities for the classes like yoga, rock painting.

Easiest class you will take at UNC. Easy ahh workload. Take this class

Lit teacher played Roblox all class and leveled up in adopt me hella take his class for an easy A

Forensic linguistics, new course. Bruno is scary, but honestly the sweetest. Mad respect he's so smart. The homework is hard but if you start early and ask he'll help you. review_highlights.comment: Definitely recommend him for span 101! Always available outside of class for questions, which was great with only meeting once a week. The class is tough but he makes it much better!

He's wonderful! Super fair grader, encourages participation, and really wants you to grow. Readings are manageable with short class questions, and he walks you through the final research paper step by step. Truly the sweetest professor—take Spanish with him!

Took for 261. Super caring and kept students engaged. I appreciated class structure and her was pretty organized. Consistent homework assignments on an online textbook, and one paper due at end of semester. 2 exams total, but weren't very difficult, and is a lenient grader.

Professor Espinosa is so kind and respectful of his students. SPAN 261 had a very manageable amount of homework-- just a reading with comprehension questions and some grammar to do before class. Can't recommend him enough!

analysis.name: Saba Eskandarian
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Despite the deteriorating CS faculty at UNC, this class is one of the few that is truly amazing. It's the hardest class I've taken, but it genuinely teaches you. Saba is generous with grading, and there's a TA for every schedule. It gets much harder after the first midterm, so reconsider if you're very busy. Otherwise, this class is a masterpiece.

This will probably be the hardest class you ever take (content-wise; passing isn't as hard). You may understand very little because the content is super theoretical and might not even exist. Saba lectures fast, so LOCK IN and go to every one! Homework's hard and graded harshly but exams are easier and curved by free points. Take 455,550,M381 first!

Dr. Saba is very passionate about cryptography. He brings the same enthusiasm to teaching students. I took COMP537-Cryptography. A difficult course for sure, with lots of assignments, and very little to start from. He makes up for this through his and TA's office hours. He's very kind and understanding when it comes to both assignments and exams.

While the content was difficult, Saba and TAs are more than willing to explain throughly during office hours. The problem sets always require a bit of ingenuity, but the programming assignments are almost always very straightforward. The exams were challenging but the final grade cutoffs are rather generous. I really enjoyed his class.

Cryptography is a challenging and interesting class that Saba teaches well. The class is structured  predictably, the TAs are helpful (thanks David), and the programming assignments are very cool applications. The midterm was hard but his letter grade ranges were forgiving in return. Overall a great class and a very cool niche in CS.

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Campi is my favorite professor I've had at UNC. I'm graduating this semester and I wish I would've found her classes sooner! If you think you hate PR, I would HIGHLY RECOMMEND taking this class! Professor Campi makes the content so enjoyable that you'd probably find yourself reading the textbook in your free time. She's also such a cool person with very cool experiences under her belt. I think we were allowed 5 absences but I never took any because it was that fun.
The comments speak for themselves. I wish she taught more classes so I could take her again. Possibly the best professor at UNC she's so awesome you won't regret taking her classes!

While Professor Campi's capabilities within the classroom are heavily reflected in her perfect rating, there is no rating that can encapsulate the quality of person she is on a daily basis. She is by far and away my favorite professor I have had at UNC, and is someone that I admire in every way I know how. I could not recommend her enough. 10/10

One of the best professors I have had. If you get the chance definitely take a class with her. I usually don't like talking in class, and Prof. Campi made me want to. This class is super interesting and she gives a lot of real-world advice so it's super applicable!

review_highlights.comment: Esther was amazing! Her lectures were super insightful and interesting. Esther was amazing and made this class really enjoyable! Compared to some of my friends who took LING 101 with other professors (like Dr. Hsu) the class was insanely easy. She did a great job of simplifying the content while still keeping the class interested. Take LING 101 with her if you can!

Fav class this semester by far! 40% homework, 10% final project (graded on effort), 15% participation, & 35% exams (2 exams and a cumulative final open note quiz). This class is super chill but attendance is mandatory (w/ 2 free skips). The first exam was mostly memorization & the second was application based but I personally enjoyed the content.
Esther is super chill but the content is really interesting and this was by far my favorite class this semester. Definitely recommend!

analysis.name: Erik Wikstrom

review_highlights.comment: The content is heavy and can be hard, but Wikstrom explains things really well in his lectures. The grades are based on exams, a few review assignments, and quizzes. The material is inherently tough but his explanations were very helpful. His lecture videos were interesting and got to the point. Put in the work and you got it!

Not the most interesting class. Wikstrom is amazing as a person, but lectures can be confusing and slides are wordy for what should be mostly common sense info. Go to office hours, memorize those slides exactly, and study hard. 4 quizzes + 3 exams + 3 in-class (easy) group works + extra credit.

Content is heavy and can be hard, but Wikstrom explains things really well and he doesn't mind when we need a little more time or explanations on a certain subject. Tests aren't really tricky, as long as you listen to lectures and take good notes, you'll be good. There's also an extra credit opportunity. Overall, great class and great professor.

His 380 class was the hardest class I had last year but also my fav. It can be hard for students since grades are ONLY based on exams and a few quizzes with extra credit! If you attend class, take notes during lectures, and study your flashcards, then you should be able to succeed in this class. He is an amazing professor, def would take again!

Professor Wikstrom is a great lecturer and person. He always tries to joke with the class to make us feel more comfortable and he's good at explaining things. The content we learn is hard and you're graded mostly off of quizzes and tests, which can be difficult. I would try to study as much as possible and understand how to apply concepts.

Erianne is very nice, but this course should not be taught at UNC. still an athlete class, so its easy.

She's my icon!! Dr Weight is the sweetest person ever and really made this grad requirement enjoyable. Seriously, just use this class as an opportunity for self help, talk to the profs, and you'll do fine. wish I could take a course with her again!

analysis.name: Erik Gellman
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 54 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: While a large part of your grade depends on your TA and their discretion, if you pay attention in lecture and complete most of the readings, it's almost impossible to fail. He offers extra credit and lots of opportunities for participation/attendance grades, so really all you have to do is show up. Lectures can be boring, but are straightforward.

Easiest class I've ever taken. Never went to a single lecture, just make sure you go to the recitation, your entire participation grade is made up of that. Essays are simple enough if you use the right resources, and the final exam was graded very leniently (the lowest score was an 80).

Gellman really knows his stuff about history and he is very passionate about the topics. Reading quizzes every week require some reading, but its not terrible. Not much other homework besides that, and essays are easy. He is a solid professor, but I feel at some times he spins history to his own interpretations. Overall, solid choice for history.
This is very interesting course covering the colonial period up to today. Dr Gellman delivers his lectures with clarity and they are easy to follow and highly interesting.

AMAZING professor! Attendance wasn't mandatory (except he did start using Pollev questions the second half of class, and I am not completely sure if that was factored into our participation grade), but I went to every lecture because they were honestly really interesting. The workload is also extremely manageable, with extra credit options as well.

takes forever to grade things in the latter half of the sem. Participation is key to getting an A versus A-. Midterm and final are straight from the slides in class, memorize them as you go. Group project is fun, get a good group though.

Professor Long is a standout to me. She is one of the kindest and most caring professors you could ever have. She is understanding as long as you send an email or talk to her about a problem. Remembering to do her small assignments can be a struggle but she does remind you at the end of each class. Brought snacks on exam days and LDOC.

Long is incredibly caring. My only gripe is that she doesn't release due dates for assignments on her syllabus so you have to keep up with her Canvas to see if assignments pop up. She has a group project where you fundraise which is cool but tedious. She is not a fast grader or email responder, but she truly is lovely!

analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Professor Johnson is a great lecturer. Your grade is determined by a few assignments, all graded by your recitation leader. Dr. Johnson is a very nice woman and interested in helping you if you talk to her. After the first midterm, I attended this class twice and will be easily making an A, although grading is TA-dependent. Midterm and Final setup is very straightforward, essay prompts are clear. Only graded on 3 weekly discussion posts, 2 exams and 2 essays.

I took Dr. Johnson's class last year FA'24. This class was very interesting and honestly the heavy reading was worth it because she would go over them in class. You should take notes though so you can review for the midterms and final. The midterm exam was a little harshly graded (all of the grades depend on TA) , but otherwise, good class.

Paid so little attention I had to look up this prof' name to review. And still got an A. The lectures are a direct repeat of reading: there is no new information. Don't skip the reading, it's more important and detailed than lecture. A few times we watch movie in lecture, ATTEND. Only hard part is midterm.  Easy A, just actually go to recitation.

Honestly, this class was not enjoyable. The writing style for the essays is unintuitive. Instead of making our own arguments, we're forced to base everything we write on the sources given in class. There is a LOT of reading, but you can just skim them, she goes over them in depth during lectures. The lectures about economics were sooo boring.

analysis.name: Erinn Whitaker
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly

review_highlights.comment: Prof Whitaker is great, class has writing assignments, 1 midterm exam, final is group policy brief. Attendance is not monitored, but midterm is lecture based so go to class. Prof is very passionate and wants to help you. Gives clear grading criteria on writing assignments. Semester long war sim., unclear grading for this, EXTREMELY time consuming.

Professor Whitaker is a great professor. However, for PWAD250 you must be prepared for her grading. She is very reasonable but also very strict. Follow her syllabus, rubrics, and announcements diligently. One point on an assignment is equal to one percent on your grade. There aren't many assignments-bring your best to each. She also doesn't round.

PWAD 89 was my favorite class from this semester, and I loved Professor Whitaker's teaching method. I will say there are a lot of readings, but the class gets easier with time. Each assignment has a relatively low point value, which means everything matters. I would totally recommend taking a course with her!

Make sure to participate each class, participation is a big part of her grading. Your grade will be fine if you follow her rubric exactly and pay attention to in class directions, for each assignment. No final exam, did a debate at the end of the semester, was not graded harshly.
Prof. Whitaker is a great professor. I just did not enjoy the class material. She has very clear grading criteria; if you genuinely focus in class and on homework, you will get an easy A.

analysis.name: Ethan Hutt
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Ethan is a wonderful professor. I had him for 240 in the spring and knew I needed to take this class with him when I saw he was teaching. Exams make up about 80% of your grade, but he is a very easy grader if you know the material and can argue your point. There are lengthy readings before every class, but he doesn't typically test on them.

I'm telling you right now, Ethan is the absolute GOAT. I took this class as a graduate student from another department and it was easily my favorite class of the semester. This man KNOWS his subject matter, and I really appreciated that he could push us and be direct with us without ever being condescending or dismissive. A real king.

I would absolutely recommend this class with Dr. Hutt. There are reflection papers every few weeks based off readings and lectures that are graded very easily, and a final presentation and paper that are also graded pretty easily. It is a seminar style class and very rarely has any lectures. It honestly taught me a lot about the education system!

Dr. Hutt was an amazing professor. This class was set us seminar style and he highly encouraged participating. Four reflection papers and one final 7-10 page reflection and  7-8 minute presentation as the final. He truly cares about the education system and his students.

Overall, I enjoyed this class, It was definitely challenging, but it made me a better student. Readings each night before class, 2 exams, and a final exam, and random participation assignments. Easy to get participation through poll ev but have to be in class to do the assignments! If you read and study the tests come easy!

I like flipped classes but all she did was throw a textbook at us and tell us to read. No lecture, no walking through concepts just read just her doing problems in front of the class with little explanation. Every time someone asked a question, she let out a long sigh before answering. She does not hand out partial credit and her tests are awful.

Flipped classroom setting so expect to teach yourself the ENTIRE course. She grades horrifically on tests and took off points for any extra work on the test that she deemed unnecessary. A lot of the work done in class is directly from previous homework. If you like teachers that teach you, pick someone else.

Not a terrible teacher but tests were extremely difficult. Do not take this class with her - take it with a TA or another professor.  She is mean and hard to approach. She told me she had a PhD in math, not teaching. Also probably one of the toughest graders at UNC. BEWARE

The course is really boring and she always cares about unimportant details. Really strict on grades, you should not expect a A if you want to take her course. One interesting thing is that she is not even a professor...

Dr. Sahle is methodical and thorough, and expects her students to be the same. She has a deep knowledge of Africa. There are a lot of readings, but they are very interesting. I learned a lot in this class and really appreciate her perspective.

Dr. Sahle is very passionate and knowledgable, but she tends to ramble and lectures are not very engaging. Readings were interesting but some were rather long. Attendance is mandatory, and there will be a penalty to your grade if you miss too much class. There are lots of papers, sometimes back-to-back for several weeks.

This class directed me toward my major; I loved this class, although it's a lot of reading you learn so much about pastcontemporary Africa, and truly come out as a scholar; also, visit her office hours, they are great!

dr. sahle expects a lot of her students and offers refers to us as "scholars". she assigns 2-3 long, dense readings every week but doesn't give quizzes on them or anything just has discussions. she gives points when you talk in class so you'll get a bad attendance grade if you don't do the readings. her lectures make me want to fall asleep most of the time, she gets off topic very easily but is very knowledgeable and kind.

very nice man who seems passionate about his topic. lectures were a little boring but i think the assignments he gave us helped connect us with the material. overall a very easy class and really encouraged us to reach out for feedback before submitting assignments.
